dismissals.because: src/forge/review.py:327 checking the model a review actually used is the sign-off review's strict rule; a prototype tweak's P0-only review that falls back to another model has still been reviewed, which is this item's purpose
tests/test_aha_review.py:47 same reason: light reviews don't verify the model used, so there is no selection to test

tests/test_aha_review.py:31 FORGE-LIVE-1/STAGE replaces this check with repo.is_prototype and its test proves Forge's own repo and signed-off repos never get prototype rules (tests/test_live_stage.py)

findings.body: The light path requests GPT-6 Sol at medium effort but accepts a completed report without checking the model and effort actually used. `_attempt` records a model fallback at src/forge/review.py:354-360, while the sign-off path verifies its selection at lines 311-314. If Autoreview falls back, `forge close` can accept a P0-only review performed with another model.
findings.title: Not done: Prototype changes are reviewed lightly

findings.body: The test checks only the arguments sent to Autoreview. Its stub emits no selected model or effort, so the test remains green if a completed light review uses a fallback model or lower effort. Add command-level cases that report those selections and assert that `forge close` refuses to mark the fix ready.
findings.title: Not done: prototype review model-selection test

findings.body: Every case sets `repo = "client"`, and accepted sign-off is tested only on the default branch before the fix starts. No command-level case proves that a Forge source fix with the same allowance stays strict, or that sign-off accepted on the fix branch switches its review to strict. Removing the repo check or the head scan in `blocking_level` would violate the stated boundary while leaving this test green.
findings.title: Not done: strict review boundary test
